clues: A harbor city wraps around a drowned river valley on the southeast coast of a vast island continent, its surf beaches facing the open ocean.
Summer afternoons can be shattered by a 'southerly buster' — a cold front racing up the coast that drops the temperature ten degrees in an hour.
A fleet of convict ships landed in 1788 at a sheltered cove, and the rough penal colony grew into the continent's oldest and largest city.
Sailors call it the finest natural harbor on earth, and its New Year's Eve fireworks are the first great show the planet sees each year.
White sail-shaped shells rise over the harbor point — the opera house with the most famous roof in the world.
